classification.difficultyReason: The rotated square requires two similarity ratios and substitution.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A right-angled triangle with sides $AB=3$, $BC=4$ and $AC=5$ has an inscribed square $PQRB$, as pictured. What is the side length of the square?

spec.description: Corner square PQRB in the 3–4–5 right triangle; routine fills omitted.
spec.mathematics: P on AB, Q on AC, R on BC; PQRB is a square.

answer.worked:
Let the square side be $x$. Then $AP=3-x$ and $PQ=x$. The triangles $ABC$ and $APQ$ are similar by AAA: they share $\angle A$ and have right angles at $B$ and $P$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AB}{AP}&=\frac{BC}{PQ},\\\frac{3}{3-x}&=\frac4x,\\3x&=4(3-x),\\7x&=12,\\x&=\frac{12}{7}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: A right-angled triangle with sides $AB=3$, $BC=4$ and $AC=5$ has an inscribed square $PQRS$, as pictured. What is the side length of the square?

spec.description: Rotated square PQRS with QR on the hypotenuse; routine fills omitted.
spec.mathematics: P on AB, S on BC; Q and R on AC; consecutive square edges perpendicular and equal.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{60}{37}$.

Use similarity in $\triangle AQP$ and $\triangle PBS$.
answer.worked:
Let the square side be $x$. By AAA, $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle AQP$ and $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle PBS$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AC}{PS}&=\frac{AB}{PB},\\\frac5x&=\frac3{PB},\\PB&=\frac{3x}{5}.\end{align*}$$
Also $AP=3-PB$, so
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AC}{AP}&=\frac{BC}{QP},\\\frac5{3-3x/5}&=\frac4x,\\5x&=12-\frac{12x}{5},\\25x&=60-12x,\\37x&=60,\\x&=\frac{60}{37}.\end{align*}$$
